domain_summary.content: Cognitive tasks assess how your child thinks, reacts, and learns about the world.

content: Infants are given tasks that measure their interest in new things, their attention to familiar and unfamiliar objects, and how they play with different types of toys
Toddlers are given tasks that examine how they explore new toys and experiences, how they solve problems, how they learn, and their ability to complete puzzles.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 7 in the cognitive domain, corresponding to an age equivalent of 8 months. This places her in the below average range, reflecting an estimated 20% delay relative to her chronological age of 10 months. During the assessment, she demonstrated difficulty with tasks requiring sustained attention and problem-solving with unfamiliar objects. These findings suggest a need for targeted cognitive stimulation to enhance exploration and adaptive learning strategies.

domain_summary.content: Receptive Communication tasks assess how well your child recognizes sounds and how much she understands spoken words and directions.

content: Infants are presented with tasks that measure their recognition of sounds, objects, and people in the environment. Many tasks involve social interactions.
Toddlers are asked to identify pictures and objects, follow simple directions, and perform social routines, such as wave bye-bye or play peek-a-boo.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 8 in the receptive communication domain, with an age equivalent of 8 months. This places her in the average range, indicating a 20% delay. Although she responds to familiar voices and looks at objects when named, there is a slight delay in following simple commands. Early intervention focusing on receptive language skills is recommended to bridge this gap.

domain_summary.content: Expressive Communication tasks assess how well your child communicates using sounds, gestures, or words.

content: Infants are observed throughout the assessment for various forms of nonverbal expression, such as smiling, jabbering expressively, using gestures, and laughing (social interaction).
Toddlers are given opportunities to use words by naming objects or pictures, putting words together, and answering questions.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 6, with an age equivalent of 6 months. This places her in the below average range, reflecting a 40% delay. Observations indicated limited vocalization and fewer instances of babbling compared to peers, suggesting the need for speech and language therapy to enhance her expressive capabilities.

domain_summary.content: Fine Motor tasks assess how well your child can use their hands and fingers to make things happen.

content: Muscle control is assessed in infants, such as visual tracking with their eyes, bringing a hand to their mouth, transferring objects from hand to hand, and reaching for and grasping an object.
Toddlers are given the opportunity to demonstrate their ability to perform fine motor tasks, such as stacking blocks, drawing simple shapes, and placing small objects (e.g., coins) in a slot.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 9, with an age equivalent of 9 months. This places her in the average range, reflecting a 10% delay. She effectively reaches for and grasps toys, although transferring objects between hands requires further development. Engaging in activities that promote bimanual coordination will support her fine motor progression.

domain_summary.content: Gross Motor tasks assess how well your child can move their body.

content: Infants are assessed for head control and their performance on activities, such as rolling over, sitting upright, and crawling motions.
Toddlers are given tasks that measure their ability to make stepping movements, support their own weight, stand, and walk without assistance.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 10, with an age equivalent of 10 months. This places her in the average range, reflecting 0% delay. Demonstrated abilities include sitting independently and initiating crawling motions. Encouragement of active play and safe exploration will continue to facilitate her gross motor development.

domain_summary.content: The Social-Emotional Scale asks caregivers to assess how their child interacts with others, expresses emotions, and responds to sensory input such as sounds, touch, and visual stimuli. This scale helps identify age-appropriate social-emotional milestones related to attachment, self-regulation, and engagement in early relationships.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina received a scaled score of 8 and a standard score of 85 on the Social-Emotional domain, placing her in the below average range and reflecting approximately a 15% delay relative to her chronological age of 10 months. According to caregiver report, she occasionally shows limited responsiveness to social cues and has difficulty with self-soothing. These observations suggest implementing social games and structured peer interactions to enhance her social-emotional capabilities.

domain_summary.content: The Adaptive Behavior Scale asks caregivers to assess their child's ability to adapt to various demands of normal daily living and become more independent.

patient_assessment.content: Sabrina's adaptive functioning was assessed through caregiver report using the Bayley-4 Adaptive Behavior Scales. Her Adaptive Behavior Composite (ADBE) score was 90, which places her performance in the average range and reflects a 10% delay compared to her chronological age.

receptive_communication.content: Sabrina earned a scaled score of 7, with an age equivalent of 8 months, reflecting a 20% delay. Observations noted difficulties in processing unfamiliar auditory cues and delayed responses to environmental sounds.

expressive_communication.content: She received a scaled score of 6, with an age equivalent of 6 months, indicating a 40% delay. Limited babbling and reduced frequency of vocalizations were observed, signaling the need for targeted communication interventions.

personal_self_care.content: In this domain, Sabrina received a scaled score of 8, with an age equivalent of 8 months, reflecting a 20% delay. She shows emerging skills in self-feeding with fingers but requires assistance with other basic self-care routines.

interpersonal_relationships.content: Sabrina earned a scaled score of 7, with an age equivalent of 8 months, reflecting a 20% delay. Her engagement in social play is limited, prompting a recommendation for interaction-enhancing activities in routine settings.

play_and_leisure.content: In this domain, Sabrina received a scaled score of 9, with an age equivalent of 9 months, indicating a 10% delay. She participates in solitary play showing interest in toys but requires further support to expand her interactive play skills.
